thread:
lina: quick note from the ingest cost spike analysis this morning: switching to watermark-aligned windows reduced duplicate writes ~9% on our sample, but introduced ~150ms added tail for some API queries

maria: interesting. can you share the metric that drove the 9% number? total token/span writes or processing CPU?

lina: it9s total write bytes + downstream parquet row counts. CPU dropped a bit too. test harness used 48h of traces with synthetic late jitter (0-8m). config: 
```yaml
processing.mode: stitch_on_write
window.align_to_watermark: true
watermark_granularity_ms: 30000
late_tolerance_ms: 300000
compaction.enabled: true
compaction.policy: first-seen
```

jon: stitch_on_write vs stitch_on_read tradeoff reminder: write-time stitching avoids reassembly work at query time but increases ingest CPU and storage churn. read-time stitching keeps writes simple but hurts query latency and query CPU.

sam: we should have explicit cost buckets for both: ingest-cost and query-cost. some tenants prefer lower query latency even if ingest cost rises. how do we expose that choice?

maria: product-wise we can surface a per-tenant preference flag: preferred_latency_tier: low/medium/high. backend maps that to windowing+stitch policy. keep default medium for now.

lina: agree. ops question: how do we ensure compaction.policy doesn9t drop spans important for cost attribution? compaction first-seen can drop later enriched copies that carry billing keys

jon: good catch. compaction needs to preserve the span with the most complete billing metadata. we can add a merge rule: prefer spans with non-empty billing_key and tenant_affinity headers

sam: merge rule implies more CPU in compaction. maybe instead we tag incoming spans with canonical_billing_key as part of preprocessor so compaction can cheaply pick the canonical one

maria: UX ask: teams want to see "effective billing key" in the console for a sample trace so they can debug attribution mismatches. can we include that in trace detail view?

lina: yes — add effective_billing_key to trace metadata after ingest. also add a diff view showing original vs canonical keys when they differ

ingest-bot: deploy bot: canary rollout of watermark-windowing started by @lina at 2026-06-03T09:02:03Z (canary=1%)

jon: rollout plan idea: 1% tenant canary with monitoring on dedupe_rate, write_bytes, query_tail_p50/p95, billing_mismatch_rate. if any trigger trips, rollback. thresholds: dedupe_rate delta > 20% or billing_mismatch_rate > 0.5% -> rollback.

sam: add cost-alert too: if write_bytes increases > 15% for a single tenant in steady-state -> auto-disable watermarking for that tenant and page SRE.

maria: also track "stitch_latency" metric for queries that request full-trace. queries that hit multiple windows should surface a warning in logs to help product teams adjust expectations

lina: implementation notes: we need a lightweight per-tenant policy lookup in the ingest hot path (memcached). heuristic producer runs in analytics to recommend lateness per-service and writes to config-store. ingest fetches config at connection setup and caches for 60s.

jon: data migration: existing stored traces were compacted under the old policy. when we flip, we'll get mixed-format traces for a while. write a compatibility layer in query engine that understands both compacted formats

sam: runbook essentials: 1) check canary dashboards, 2) if billing_mismatch spikes, switch canary back to 0% and run the billing reclassification job on affected tenants, 3) if query tail latency spikes, toggle stitch_on_read for the affected tenant as temporary fix

maria: timeline: RFC + automation PR this week, canary next week assuming no blocking infra work. engineering estimate: 2s backend eng + 1 infra + 1 UX over 3 sprints for a full rollout and console bits

lina: I9ll draft the RFC with config schema, heuristics producer spec, rollout steps, and the runbook. ping me for review. thanks all. :thumbsup:
